fair_value.method: Horizon (Sep-2027) value. Forward NTM EV/EBITDA (~$717M x 5.75x, ~$150M horizon net debt, 106M diluted shares -> $37.5, weight 0.45), forward P/E (NTM EPS ~$3.94 x 9.5x -> $37.4, weight 0.35), and a long-term-deck NAV cross-check ($5.00/lb Cu, Furnas risked on Ero's 60% attributable basis, 1.0x P/NAV -> $26, weight 0.20). The blend is ~$35.2, slightly below the $37.87 price.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: NTM at horizon (Q4-27 to Q3-28): copper ~80 kt (filed outlook is 75-85 kt for 2027 and 80-90 kt for 2028, haircut for the guidance-miss history) = 176M lb x ($6.05 realized - $2.25 C1) = ~$670M; Xavantina ~55 koz x ~$2,500/oz margin (gold ~$4,000) = ~$137M; less ~$90M G&A/exploration/royalties -> EBITDA ~$717M. Multiple 5.75x, discounted from 6x because the deck sits near cycle highs and for Brazil/execution risk -> EV $4.12B; less ~$150M horizon net debt ($452.7M at Q2-26); 106M diluted shares -> $37.5. Realized $6.05/lb: Ero realized $5.78 in Q2-26; LME spot is ~$6.5-6.6; bank 2027 views run from Citi ~$5.44 to Goldman $6.26.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS ~$3.94: EBITDA $717M - D&A ~$165M - interest ~$30M = ~$522M pretax, ~20% tax (SUDENE) -> ~$418M / 106M shares. 9.5x, the low end of the 9-12x mid-cycle range, because earnings are on a near-peak copper deck. Cross-check: 2027E at 77 kt is ~$3.65 EPS; consensus 2027E ~$4.79 assumes a higher deck.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: NAV: long-term copper $5.00/lb, gold $3,500/oz, 8% real discount rate; Caraiba + Tucuma + Xavantina unlevered FCF ~$380M/yr over ~12 years -> ~$2.85B; Furnas: PEA NPV8 $2.0B is on a 100% basis at $4.60 Cu, Ero's 60% is ~$1.2B, less the Vale up-to-11% construction carry = ~$1.1B, risked at ~40% (PEA stage, PFS 2027, FID ~2029) -> ~$0.45B; corporate costs -$0.3B; net debt -$0.45B -> equity ~$2.55B = ~$24/share today, rolled forward at 8% to ~$26 at the horizon, at 1.0x P/NAV (peers 0.82-0.95x on $4.00-4.50 decks, or ~1.1-1.2x for de-risked producers; Ero sits between them because it is single-country with an execution record). Sensitivity: each +$0.50/lb long-term is ~+$6/share.

bear.story: Copper falls back to a ~$5.00-5.25/lb realized price (below Citi's ~$5.44 2027 base case) as LME stocks build and tariff-driven US stockpiling reverses. Ero misses again (2027 ~72 kt; the Pilar shaft or Tucuma filtration slips) and the BRL strengthens once the collars expire at end-2027. EBITDA ~$480M x 5x, less ~$300M net debt -> ~$21.

base.story: Copper realizes ~$5.75-6.30/lb (inside the Citi-to-Goldman range), 2027 production ~77-82 kt at C1 ~$2.25 (BRL collars with a 5.40 floor through Dec-2027 limit the cost creep), net debt ~$100-200M at the horizon, capital returns start, and the Furnas PFS is published. The stock trades at ~5.75-6x NTM EBITDA, in the mid/high $30s.

bull.story: Copper extends to $7-7.50/lb on deficits (Grasberg/Kamoa-Kakula delays, US stockpiling), Ero hits the top of the 75-85 kt outlook, reaches net cash by mid-2027 with a buyback or dividend, and a strong Furnas PFS re-rates the second growth leg. NTM EBITDA ~$1B at 6x -> high $50s.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$23 equity is ~$2.45B and EV ~$2.6-2.7B with $150-300M net debt, about 3.8x 2027 EBITDA even at $5.00/lb copper. That level implies either copper sustained below ~$4.75/lb, which is under every current bank 2027 forecast (Citi ~$5.44, Goldman $6.26 after its June-2026 raise), or a fundamental operating failure: Tucuma filtration not lifting throughput, the Pilar/Caraiba volume step-up slipping, 2027 guidance set well below the 75-85 kt outlook, or a Brazil fiscal/royalty shock. Any of these breaks the deleveraging and FCF-inflection thesis; ordinary 50-60%-vol noise should not.

Pilar external shaft commissioning (drives the Caraiba volume step-up)

key_uncertainties: Copper price: LME ~$6.5-6.6/lb is near records; bank 2027 views run from ~$5.44 (Citi base) to $6.26/lb (Goldman, raised June 2026). Each $0.50/lb is ~$85-90M of EBITDA, or ~$4-5/share
Execution: three years of guidance misses; Tucuma throughput/filtration; Pilar shaft timing and Caraiba grade sequencing
Brazil: election, fiscal/royalty policy, and BRL cost pressure after the $450M collars (floor 5.40, cap 6.34) expire in Dec-2027
Furnas: PEA stage on Ero's 60% earn-in, with Vale's up-to-11% construction carry; PFS due 2027, FID ~2029
Capital allocation after deleveraging (buybacks/dividends vs Furnas spend)
reasoning: ERO is Ero Copper (Brazil: Caraiba and Tucuma copper, Xavantina gold, 60% earn-in on Vale's Furnas). Round 2 applies the supervisor's evidence-backed corrections. (1) Goldman's 2027 forecast is $13,800/t (~$6.26/lb, raised June 2026, which I verified), not $10,750/t, so my bear anchor was stale. (2) The Furnas PEA NPV8 of $2.0B is on a 100% basis (verified); Ero's attributable ~$1.1-1.2B, risked, is ~$0.45B, not my $0.9B. (3) My 1.15x P/NAV was too generous for a single-country mid-tier: peers trade 0.82-0.95x on conservative decks, though Skillings also cites ~1.1-1.2x for de-risked producers of comparable scale, so I use 1.0x on a $5.00 deck. (4) Ero realized $5.78/lb in Q2-26 (verified in the MD&A), so I cut my realized deck from $6.20 to $6.05. I stay a bit above the supervisor's $6.00 because LME spot is ~$6.55 and Goldman is at $6.26. (5) The BRL collars run to Dec-2027 (verified), so I use a 2027 C1 of $2.25. (6) The filed outlook is 75-85 kt (2027) and 80-90 kt (2028) with ~106M diluted shares (verified). Because the horizon price will be set on NTM cash flows, I moved the multiples legs to NTM (~80 kt): EV/EBITDA $37.5 and P/E $37.4. The NAV leg falls from $30 to $26 because the lower Furnas value and lower multiple both reduce it; I disagree with the supervisor that they offset. I cut its weight to 0.20 since the horizon price is driven by cash-flow multiples. Blended fair value is $35.2 (from $36.5), slightly below spot. I did not move the ladder centre down by the same amount, for two reasons. First, the downside anchors were revised up: every bank 2027 view is now >=$5.44, and the collars reduce the cost risk. Second, spot copper sits above my deck and the sell side is marking targets up (CIBC C$56, NBF C$55). The median stays ~$37 and P(>=38) is ~0.48, essentially unchanged. Width is ~47% log-vol: below the 64% realized, far above large-cap base rates because ERO is roughly 2x levered to copper. The extreme left tail is slightly fatter than lognormal for single-country and copper-crash risk; the bear case is a little less likely (0.22) and a little less severe ($21). Scenario mean ~$38.7. Research used about 5 follow-up queries/fetches; no option data was used.

revisions.why: The NAV leg fell (Furnas 100%-basis correction and a 1.0x not 1.15x P/NAV) and the realized copper deck was trimmed to $6.05. Moving the multiples legs to NTM (2028 volumes) partly offset this.
